pages.summary: This newcomer-first runbook connects the operator console and customer portal: respond to durable alerts, correlate bounded operational evidence, reconcile offline commercial documents, follow exclusive-machine access through expiry, and use the role-safe guide diagnostics page.

blocks.text: Start with the right surface

blocks.title: One event, two audiences
blocks.text: A durable source event can appear as an actionable operator alert and as a tenant-scoped customer notification. Reading or dismissing a message does not erase the source receipt, and a delivery retry does not create another business event.
Recipe 1: triage an alert and confirm the customer message

items: Operator: open Alerts, inspect Critical and High items first, and retain the correlation or source receipt before changing anything. Do not assume a sortable table or a separate detail dialog.
Operator: inspect the current evidence, then acknowledge ownership. Assign it to a named responder; use a bounded silence only when a maintenance window explains the signal.
Operator: resolve only after the typed condition has recovered. Resolution closes the alert lifecycle but preserves its evidence.
Customer: open Notifications in the enterprise portal, confirm the message belongs to the expected order or lease, follow its safe action, and choose Mark as read.
If email, SMS, or webhook delivery fails, continue with the in-app record and investigate the operator DeliveryDeadLetter alert.

blocks.text: Recipe 2: correlate events, metrics, alerts, and audit

steps.title: Operational event
steps.text: The component emits bounded JSON with a stable event code, outcome, component, time, and correlation receipt.

steps.title: Metric update
steps.text: A counter, gauge, or latency series changes using low-cardinality labels; tenant, user, lease, and request identifiers never become metric labels.

steps.title: Typed rule
steps.text: A state or metric rule detects the condition. Rules do not parse human log prose.

steps.title: Durable alert
steps.text: The notification authority deduplicates the condition and opens or updates the operator record.

steps.title: Audit correlation
steps.text: For a consequential mutation, the immutable audit receipt explains actor class, prior state, next state, decision, and result.

blocks.title: Logs explain; they do not grant authority
blocks.text: Use the correlation receipt to join the alert, operational event, adapter call, and audit record. Never paste raw logs, tokens, document bytes, prompts, model output, SSH material, or callback bodies into a ticket or the guide.
Recipe 3: complete the hybrid offline workflow

steps.title: Configure online
steps.text: The customer selects the service, SLA, project, and requested expiry; the server derives tenant and purchaser identity.

steps.title: Prepare packet
steps.text: The operator applies the immutable quote and approved policy, obtains internal approval, and releases only renderer-verified print artifacts.

steps.title: Execute offline
steps.text: The customer prints the PDF and follows the existing physical seal, treasury collection, and invoice process.

steps.title: Upload evidence
steps.text: The customer requests a short-lived upload grant. The object store and scanner report the verified digest and safety result; the browser does not choose the object reference.

steps.title: Reconcile
steps.text: A reviewer who did not submit the evidence accepts or rejects the exact digest. Rejection keeps history and requests a replacement revision.

steps.title: Fulfill
steps.text: The operator creates the opaque entitlement only after every policy-required agreement, payment, invoice, identity, and approval item is accepted.

blocks.answer: Confirm the typed condition has recovered, then correlate the alert's source or correlation receipt with the bounded operational event, relevant metric, and immutable audit record. Customer read state or a successful delivery alone is not recovery evidence.

steps.title: Fence writer
steps.text: Stop or isolate the old controller and restore data into clean infrastructure.

steps.title: Raise epoch
steps.text: Start a controller with a strictly newer LUNANEXA_CONTROLLER_EPOCH.

steps.text: Set LUNANEXA_RECONCILIATION_ONLY=1 and inspect /v1/recovery/plan.

pages.title: Debug controller, ingress, and fencing failures
pages.summary: Start from the public symptom and preserve the trust boundary. Most controller failures fall into process health, trusted ingress/authentication, configuration/rendering, network policy, or epoch fencing.

blocks.symptom: The console cannot load and the controller health endpoint is unavailable.
likely_causes: Controller pod is not ready or crash-looping.
Rendered environment, secret reference, volume, or PostgreSQL URL is missing.
Ingress route or NetworkPolicy does not reach the controller.
The browser is bypassing the trusted ingress path.
checks: Inspect Kubernetes pod status, readiness events, and bounded controller logs.
Confirm every required placeholder was resolved and management node placement is correct.
Probe /health from an allowed management pod, then through trusted ingress.
Check PostgreSQL readiness and controller connection without printing the database URL.
resolution: Fix the specific render, storage, database, or routing dependency and let Kubernetes restart normally.
Keep direct public controller access blocked; correct ingress or policy instead of widening exposure.
escalate_when: The controller repeatedly corrupts or rejects durable state.
Recovery requires a restore or epoch change.

likely_causes: A newer controller already advanced the durable fencing epoch.
An old process, assignment, or restored snapshot is attempting to write.
checks: Inspect the current durable epoch and active controller identity.
Confirm no old controller process or pod remains reachable.
Open /v1/recovery/plan from the newer reconciliation-only controller.
resolution: Do not lower or reuse the epoch. Fence the stale writer and continue recovery from the newer durable epoch.
escalate_when: Two live controllers appear to hold authority.
The durable store and observed deployment disagree about the current epoch.

blocks.symptom: Requests return Unauthenticated through a browser or remote client.

A remote client attempted to use X-LunaNexa-Subject, which is loopback-only.

Inspect ingress authentication result and header overwrite policy.
Verify the controller sees the intended trusted network peer.

blocks.symptom: The administrator guide diagnostics page is unavailable, stale, or missing evidence.

The server-only skill manifest or coursebook evidence index is invalid or older than its freshness threshold.
The internal HTTPS diagnostics route, controller health, operator alert, node, lease, or reconciliation endpoint is unavailable.

Use the correlation receipt from admin.html to find the bounded GuideAdminDiagnosticRequest audit event.
Confirm the identity proxy signs the documented method/path/actor/role/timestamp payload without printing its HMAC key.

The runtime leaks internal paths or credentials in its public error.

pages.title: Debug workspace authority and PostgreSQL
pages.summary: For a browser HTTP 401, reload or sign in again as prompted and let the portal recover its session without replaying a lifecycle mutation. A 403 remains an authorization failure. Other access failures require checking: subject mapping, lifecycle state, tenant scope, lease time/capability, request ownership, rate/concurrency, or database authority does not match.

likely_causes: The asserted subject is not recognized or ingress identity mapping changed.
User is invited, suspended, or revoked rather than active.
Grant is absent, revoked, expired, or belongs to another tenant.
Lease is requested, expired, revoked, wrong capability, or outside its time window.
Authority changed between self-read and admission.
checks: Read /v1/workspace/self through the same trusted identity path.
Inspect exact user, grant, tenant, lease state, capability, starts, and expiry in the console.
Check immutable prior/next audit events for recent activation, suspension, revocation, or end.
resolution: Use the typed operator lifecycle route to correct the authoritative record. Do not forge a subject header or edit the state file manually.
escalate_when: A revoked subject can still invoke or one tenant can observe another tenant's workload.

likely_causes: The capability's held-request concurrency is in use.
The rolling one-hour request limit is exhausted.
A prior controller crash conservatively holds a reservation until its bounded deadline.
checks: Inspect active workload status and cancellation ownership.
Review the .admissions state or PostgreSQL snapshot through operator tooling—not by deleting it.
Confirm deadlines and completed/cancelled releases are reconciling.
resolution: Wait for bounded release, cancel an owned active workload, or issue a reviewed lease change. Do not clear counters by deleting durable evidence.
escalate_when: A completed workload never releases held concurrency after recovery.

blocks.symptom: The controller cannot start or mutate PostgreSQL-backed authority.
likely_causes: Database URL, TLS verification, network policy, role privilege, or schema version is wrong.
Migration was not run with owner authority.
A normalized projection constraint rejected the transaction.
checks: Probe PostgreSQL readiness from the controller network boundary.
Run the idempotent migration command with a secret reference and owner role.
Inspect schema_migrations and projection row counts after restore.
Review the bounded database error without printing the URL or password.
resolution: Correct the secret-provider value, TLS trust, network rule, role, or migration; rerun the transaction after the schema is valid.
escalate_when: Snapshot and normalized projections diverge or a failed projection commits partial state.

pages.title: Public error and state reference
pages.summary: Typed codes communicate which boundary rejected work. Use the code and retryability, then follow the linked diagnostic path; do not infer internal topology from a bounded public message.

rows: Unauthenticated
Required scoped credential or verified subject is absent/invalid
Correct the trusted identity or credential path; do not retry blindly.
Unauthorized
Authenticated authority lacks the requested scope
Use the right scoped credential or request an explicit grant.
WorkspaceAccessDenied
Subject, user, grant, tenant, lease, capability, or ownership does not authorize the request
Inspect /v1/workspace/self and authoritative lifecycle records.
WorkspaceConcurrencyExceeded
Capability's held concurrent requests are in use
Wait, cancel an owned workload, or review lease capacity.
WorkspaceRateExceeded
Rolling one-hour request limit is exhausted
Wait for the window or apply a reviewed lease change.
WorkloadAlreadyActive
Same active workload/idempotency scope already exists
Query the existing workload; do not launch a duplicate.
DeadlineExceeded
Queue or runtime deadline expired
Treat as terminal for that request; reassess deadline/capacity before a new logical operation.
RuntimeUnavailable
Selected serving adapter failed or disappeared
Inspect artifact, image, readiness, route, TLS, and adapter compatibility.
StaleControllerEpoch
A newer durable controller fenced this writer or assignment
Fence the stale process and reconcile under the newer epoch.
NodeUnavailable
Node is absent or already bound by incompatible authority
Inspect enrollment, heartbeat, lease, and current node mode.
Blocked deployment
Preflight evidence or capacity is missing
Read typed findings; supply reviewed evidence before retrying.
CancelledByCaller
The authenticated owner cancelled the workload
No runtime-failure escalation unless cancellation was unexpected.

blocks.title: Public errors are intentionally bounded
blocks.text: They do not contain node addresses, filesystem paths, container IDs, provider credentials, stack traces, or internal topology. Operators use correlated audit and protected logs for deeper diagnosis.
Search the exact error: first call and portal access

rows: TrialApiKeyRejected
The single trial key was already issued; another issuance is rejected.
Reveal or copy the active saved key in Account & API keys. Expired or revoked keys cannot be retrieved, and expiry does not automatically create another trial.
PortalAccessDenied
Your selected organization membership does not authorize this action.
Check the selected organization and ask its administrator for the required role; signing into the operator site does not grant a portal role.

This admission path requires an effective commercial master agreement.
Check the commercial agreement with your administrator. Private-cloud administrator-granted workspaces must use the configured private-cloud path, not fabricated contract evidence.
HTTP 401
Authentication failed; this does not uniquely mean a wrong URL.

Use the configured API entrance and correct non-expired scoped key. For a browser session, reload or sign in again as prompted. Authentication recovery must not replay Start, Stop, order or payment actions. Never share the secret.
HTTP 403
The requested action, model or tenant is outside current authority.
Check the exact public code, selected organization, active lease and allowed model aliases.
HTTP 409
The request conflicts with current state; this does not uniquely mean a lost trial key.
Read the exact code and refresh state before retrying. Do not repeat non-repeatable issuance or create duplicate orders.
HTTP 429
Rate, concurrency or total quota may be exhausted.
Check request usage and the exact code. Wait for an applicable rate window or running request; a total allowance does not refill automatically.
Network timeout
No reliable result was received; a mutation may still have committed.
Check connectivity and refresh the operation state. Reuse the supported idempotency identity rather than creating a duplicate payment, order or workload.

blocks.text: Support needs the public error code, action, approximate time and non-secret receipt/correlation identifier. Do not include API keys, SSH certificates, private keys, provider tokens, raw prompts or customer content. The error explanation link should lead to this page, not an internal log.

blocks.answer: No. Runtime termination, company resource ownership, personal storage and machine-lease cleanup have separate lifecycles.

pages.title: ComfyUI basics: run an approved workflow
pages.summary: Open the workflow supplied for your ComfyUI profile, understand its connected nodes, submit once and save the result. Hosted workspaces and the public native H3 workspace use different profiles.

blocks.text: A workflow is a saved graph of nodes: each node accepts inputs, performs a step and passes its result along a connection. Start with the workflow supplied for your exact workspace and model. A generic Stable Diffusion checkpoint graph is not a native H3 video graph.

items.title: Choose the correct workspace
items.text: Use the signed-in portal for a personal workspace. The separately published port-5005 workspace is anonymous and shared; do not upload private files there.

items.title: Load the supplied workflow
items.text: Choose a template or saved workflow for the model profile shown in this workspace. Keep its approved nodes, model selection and connection settings. Do not reuse the retired public /h3/v1/ graph in native H3.

items.title: Review inputs and submit once
items.text: Enter your prompt and any references supported by this template. Use its preset dimensions, duration and sampling values for the first attempt. Submit with the workspace's run control once, then observe the same queued task.

items.title: Follow the task to completion
items.text: Personal video profiles with the 视频任务 panel keep a durable task record; reopen or reconnect the original task after a transient disconnect. The public native queue is a different mechanism. Do not create another job merely because the page disconnected.

items.title: Save workflow and output
items.text: A completed task should provide a usable image or video. Download the media, check that it opens or plays, and export the workflow JSON. A queue entry or progress bar alone is not a finished result.

blocks.symptom: The workflow has missing nodes, an unavailable model or a failed task.
likely_causes: The graph targets a different model/runtime profile.
Workspace authority expired, or its serving provider is unavailable.
The requested dimensions, duration or reference format are unsupported.
checks: Reload a template supplied by this workspace and read the exact task error.
In a personal workspace, check the selected organization and current access; in the public workspace, check its native queue.
Keep the original task identifier when reconnecting after a lost response.
resolution: Use the supported profile or ask the operator to restore its dependency. Hosted users must not install custom nodes or change server credentials.

blocks.title: Performance depends on the profile
blocks.text: Duration, resolution, sampling and current load affect completion time. Earlier generation timings belong to their recorded engine and preset; they are not a speed promise for the current native H3 route.

blocks.question: What should you do after a connection drops during a job?
blocks.answer: Find the original task and check its result before submitting anything else. A lost browser response does not prove that execution stopped.

items.text: Download needed files before machine expiry or End access early. Contact the operator in advance if more time is needed; there is no guaranteed extension or self-service machine-renewal action.

items.text: Access is revoked and the approved tenant accounts, containers and writable volumes are cleaned in stages. A node returns to managed scheduling only after current cleanup evidence is accepted; uncertainty means quarantine.

blocks.text: Machine expiry is not an instant whole-disk wipe or a backup guarantee. Personal hosted volumes follow their retention policy and can survive logout or container restart. Public-workspace files are shared. Keep your own verified copy of anything important.

pages.title: Planned: autoscaling and batch job queues
pages.summary: Two fleet-scale features — capacity that grows and shrinks by itself, and queues of batch jobs — and why 能源谷“创未来”生态街区's current product contract deliberately excludes both. This page explains what would have to be proven first, and the predictable-overload behavior you get today.
pages.audience: Users planning large or bursty workloads, and operators who need to explain the fixed-fleet behavior

blocks.text: Autoscaling means the fleet adds or removes machines as demand changes, without a human involved. Batch queues mean you hand over a pile of jobs — render these ten thousand images, process this dataset — and the system works through them while you sleep. Both are real cloud features, and both are deliberately absent from 能源谷“创未来”生态街区's current contract.

blocks.title: Not available today — by explicit decision
blocks.text: The current product contract lists batch jobs, task groups, spot queues, and an autonomous autoscaler as out of scope. They are Phase 6 candidates in the expansion plan: each would arrive as its own program with its own product contract, security boundary, service objective, and acceptance campaign — not as a quiet feature flag.
What you would be able to do

steps.title: Describe the work with bounds
steps.text: Submit a job queue or a scaling rule with explicit limits: maximum nodes, deadline, and priority — never an open-ended claim on the fleet.

steps.title: The fleet decides within evidence
steps.text: Scaling and scheduling decisions come from measured capacity and health, with exclusive-lease fencing always respected.

steps.title: Predictable endings
steps.text: Every job ends in a typed terminal state with a receipt — completed, failed with a stated reason, or cancelled. Never limbo.

blocks.text: What has to be proven first

items: The four-node internal pilot and the shared production foundations (Phases 1–2 of the expansion plan) come first.
An autoscaler must never override health, security, placement, or exclusive-lease fencing — policy outranks demand.
Retry caps, circuit breakers, and typed terminal failure reasons are prerequisites: a fleet must fail predictably rather than burn leases on bad work.

blocks.text: What you get today instead

Today's fleet is fixed and honest about it. Admission uses the active policy, authorization and runtime capacity. When its bounded capacity is full, work queues or receives a typed rejection. Private-model keys may have no request-count cap, and runtime_concurrency: 0 adds no execution semaphore; neither disables resource safety or lease expiry. For interactive and inference work this predictability is a feature: your lease means what it says.

Approved deployment-owned source; selected managed nodes verify assignment-bound bytes

blocks.title: Mountable is not safe for multiple writers
blocks.text: RWX does not authorize two editors to write one workspace simultaneously. The gateway uses persisted writer ownership, waits for old pods to stop before release and returns StorageBusy, StorageMigrationRequired or StorageNotConfigured when the evidence does not permit launch.

Future tenant volume management and image publishing require their own quota, ownership, migration, deletion and recovery evidence. Machine-lease cleanup affects its approved tenant boundary; it is not an automatic wipe of the management model store.

blocks.answer: No. Existing volume class and node affinity are checked; an incompatible placement requires an explicit reviewed migration.

pages.title: Planned: an in-portal chat playground
pages.summary: The simplest possible first call: pick a model, pick your API key, type a message, see the answer — without leaving the portal or writing any code. Public model clouds offer this as an online debugging panel; 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 may add it as a thin layer over the same request contract. Today, the workbench is the way.
pages.audience: New users who want to verify a model and a key in ten seconds, before writing any integration code

blocks.text: A chat playground is the smallest possible try-it: a panel where you pick a model, pick one of your API keys, type a message, and read the answer. No SDK, no terminal, no setup. It is the feature beginners reach for when they just want to confirm that their key works — and it may come to the 能源谷“创未来”生态街区 portal in exactly that spirit.

blocks.title: Not available today
blocks.text: The portal has no chat panel today. The workbench already sends real model calls from the browser with quota visibility and receipts — and trial visitors can try a prompt there without even creating a key, using the trial session.
